title: Brain and Blood Extraction for Immunostaining, Protein, and RNA Measurements
author: Nancy E. Ruiz-Uribe
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-838/v1
materials: For RNA analysis, prepare a tube containing Trizol or a lysis buffer with an RNAase inhibitor of preference 3 . For protein extraction, prepare extraction buffer in a 50 mL conical tube containing 1 mM AESBF (or other appropriate proteinase inhibitors), 1 tablet of cOmplete and 2 mL of RIPA buffer and dilute 1:25 with 1X PBS. Place half brain inside a clean Dounce homogenizer and homogenize the brain with 500 uL of extraction buffer. Use small strokes to avoid bubbles. A total of 20-30 strokes should be enough to homogenize the tissue. With a pipette, transfer the homogenized tissue to an Eppendorf and keep on ice. Wash the homogenizer with MiliQ water between samples. Sonicate tubes on water for 10 minutes. Transfer samples to a 4ºC centrifuge, and centrifuge at 14000 rpm (table top centrifuge) for 30 min. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube and if desired, the pellet can be stored for further processing. If extracting protein or RNA from cerebral microvessels is of interest, follow this detailed protocol on extracting cerebral microvessels from cortex 4 . After sample preparation: · Proceed with preferred protocol for protein measurement (Figure 2). We use Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (ThermoFisher CAT No. 23225) · If performing RNA extraction, process samples as quickly as possible and clean all surfaces with RNAzap (ThermoFisher, CAT No. AM9780). Proceed with preferred protocol for RNA extraction. (Figure 3) CRITICAL STEP: The extraction and sectioning of the brain has to be performed as quickly as possible in order to ensure the least amount of RNA or protein degradation.
4-5 hours, depending on the number of brains.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse with pentobarbital
steps.instruction: Inject pentobarbital intraperitoneally at 10 mg kg⁻¹ to achieve lethal anesthesia.

steps.title: Collect blood via cardiac puncture
steps.instruction: Restrain the mouse by scruffing the back so the body hangs vertically. Insert a 22‑25 G needle attached to a 3 mL syringe just under the ribs at the mid‑line, aiming for the heart at the elbow level. Gently withdraw the plunger until blood flows; if no flow, move the needle slightly up or down and retry. Collect 1–2 mL of blood without applying extra back‑pressure. Transfer the blood immediately to an EDTA‑containing vacutainer. If the blood is intended for RNA extraction, add Trizol LS at a ratio of 3 parts Trizol LS to 1 part blood, then process immediately or snap‑freeze. If the blood remains >1 min in the syringe before EDTA transfer, coat the syringe interior with a small amount of EDTA. Store samples at –80 °C or process fresh.

substeps.instruction: Restrain mouse by scruffing; keep body vertical.
Insert 22‑25 G needle with 3 mL syringe under ribs at mid‑line, heart level.
Withdraw plunger until blood appears; adjust needle position if needed.
Collect 1–2 mL blood; avoid extra back‑pressure.
Transfer blood to EDTA vacutainer tube.
For RNA: add 3 parts Trizol LS per 1 part blood; process immediately or snap‑freeze.
If >1 min before EDTA transfer, add a small amount of EDTA to syringe interior.
Store at –80 °C or proceed to RNA extraction.

steps.title: Transcardial perfusion with PBS
steps.instruction: Place the mouse on its back on a grate over a rectangular bucket and tape all four limbs to the grate. Make a ventral incision from below the ribs to the upper chest to expose the cavity, attach hemostats to the ribs and retract them to fully expose the heart. Insert a 21 G needle connected to a perfusion pump filled with 1X PBS into the left ventricle, then make a small cut in the right atrium. Pump 1X PBS until the outflow from the atrial cut runs clear; the liver should change from deep red to a paler shade, indicating adequate perfusion. Do not follow with 4 % PFA, as half of the brain will be used for protein work.

substeps.instruction: Position mouse on back on grate; tape fore‑ and hind‑limbs.
Cut from below ribs to upper chest to open cavity.
Attach hemostats to ribs and retract to expose heart.
Insert 21 G needle (perfusate: 1X PBS) into left ventricle.
Make small incision in right atrium.
Pump 1X PBS until fluid exiting atrial cut is clear; note liver color change.
Stop perfusion; do not perfuse with 4 % PFA.

steps.title: Dissect brain and fix half
steps.instruction: After PBS perfusion, the brain should appear pale through the cranial window. Remove the cranial window with forceps, decapitate with scissors, and cut away neck muscles and skin covering the cranium. Insert scissors through the foramen magnum and gently cut the cranial bone posteriorly toward the rostral side, taking care not to damage the brain. Remove lateral bone flaps with forceps, tilt the brain upward with curved forceps, and slide it out into a petri dish placed in an ice bath. Wash the brain in ice‑cold 1X PBS to remove debris. Halve the brain sagittally with a clean razor blade. Using curved forceps, separate cortex from hippocampus (or dissect other regions as needed). Immerse one half (for immunostaining) in 4 % PFA and fix overnight at 4 °C; after 24 h transfer this half to 30 % sucrose. Snap‑freeze the other half in liquid nitrogen or process immediately for RNA or protein extraction. If immediate processing is not possible, homogenize the tissue immediately (Dounce homogenizer or bead mill) in the appropriate buffer with RNase or protease inhibitors, then snap‑freeze and store at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Confirm brain pallor; remove cranial window with forceps.
Decapitate; cut neck muscles and skin.
Insert scissors through foramen magnum; cut cranial bone toward rostral side.
Remove lateral bone flaps; expose brain.
Tilt brain upward with curved forceps; slide out into ice‑bath petri dish.
Wash brain in ice‑cold 1X PBS.
Section brain sagittally with razor blade.
Separate cortex from hippocampus (or other regions) with curved forceps.
Place one half in 4 % PFA; fix overnight (≈24 h) at 4 °C.
Transfer fixed half to 30 % sucrose solution.
Snap‑freeze other half in liquid nitrogen or process immediately for RNA/protein.
If processing delayed: homogenize immediately in buffer with RNase/protease inhibitors, snap‑freeze, store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare cryoprotection solution and embed brain
steps.instruction: Prepare cryoprotection solution by mixing 150 g sucrose, 200 mL 1X PBS, and 150 mL ethylene glycol; bring the final volume to 500 mL with 1X PBS and store at 4 °C. Remove the fixed half from the sucrose solution, place it in a petri dish, and position it (coronal or sagittal) in a metallic cryotome holder using OCT compound as adhesive. Ensure the brain is oriented straight and parallel to the blade. Freeze the holder in the cryotome, trim away excess OCT until the brain surface is exposed, and slice at 30 µm (or desired thickness). Collect each slice into PBS, then alternate placement of slices into six pre‑labeled tubes (or as many as needed), each containing 1.7 mL of the same cryoprotection solution. Store the tubes at 4 °C until further use.

substeps.instruction: Mix 150 g sucrose, 200 mL 1X PBS, 150 mL ethylene glycol; add 1X PBS to 500 mL total.
Store cryoprotection solution at 4 °C.

Position brain in cryotome holder with OCT adhesive; orient straight, blade‑parallel.
Freeze holder inside cryotome.
Trim OCT until brain surface visible.

Submerge each slice in PBS, then place alternately into six tubes (or appropriate number) each containing 1.7 mL cryoprotection solution.
Label tubes accordingly; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Mount slices and perform immunostaining
steps.instruction: Retrieve a tube of slices stored at 4 °C. Transfer slices onto a petri dish containing 1X PBS and mount 3–6 slices per glass slide using a brush, ensuring they lie flat and unfurled. Leave margin space for a liquid‑blocking marker. Allow slides to dry completely, then draw a rectangle with the liquid‑blocking marker. Wash slides six times with PBS for 5 min each. Prepare blocking solution by adding 250 µL goat serum and 50 µL 10 % Triton X‑100 to 5 mL total volume with 1X PBS. Block slides for 30 min. Aspirate blocking solution and apply primary antibody diluted 1:500 (or as recommended) in blocking solution; incubate overnight at 4 °C in a humid chamber (wet paper towel). The next day, aspirate primary antibody and wash slides three times with 1X PBS for 5 min each. Apply secondary antibody diluted 1:500 in blocking solution; incubate 2 h at room temperature in a light‑shielded area with a wet paper towel. Aspirate secondary antibody and wash three times with 1X PBS. If desired, apply counterstain (e.g., Methoxy‑X04 diluted 1:250 in 1X PBS) for 15 min at room temperature, then wash twice with 80 % ethanol. Allow slides to dry thoroughly, then mount with a preferred mounting medium (e.g., ProLong Gold).
